description: FLOWSA is a Python package developed and maintained by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency to attribute resources (environmental, economic and material), emissions, wastes and losses, together called flows, to industrial and final-use sectors, generally by North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) codes. Its models capture flows between the environment and sectors and transfers between sectors, allocating primary data sources to industries with secondary data and activity-to-sector mappings. Version 2.0.0 (2023) added primary data sources, sector attribution models, visualisation functions, attribution methods and sector codes, and the Zenodo archive holds version 2.2.0 of 10 November 2025 under the MIT licence. FLOWSA outputs are the environmental inputs to the USEEIO models through the useeior package, and the code and documentation are on GitHub. Access is free. Caveats: coverage is the United States, and attributions depend on the chosen secondary data and mapping choices. For simulation it provides sector-level resource use and emissions for input-output and life cycle models of the U.S. economy. Related catalogue records include USEEIO, the Toxics Release Inventory and the Manufacturing Energy Consumption Survey.
